layer_1_what_it_is.what_it_is: The library hands the method the exact passage to read — already broken into pieces, with a record of where every word came from. It's the join between the library (what we hold) and the method (how we read it).
layer_1_what_it_is.why_it_matters: If the method reads a loose, retyped copy, it can drift from the real text — and it did: the copy we coded from flattened the ending of Mark, dropping 'for they were afraid.' A checkout hands over the verbatim words plus their address, so every reading traces back to the real passage.

the_process.you ask for: a passage — e.g. 'Mark chapter 16, the World English Bible'
the_process.the library does: finds it · checks it's really in our collection, already broken into pieces, and OK to use · packages the exact words with a record of where each came from
the_process.you get back: a small, sealed package of the verbatim passage the method reads — with its address baked in

the_contrast.heading: What the coder saw vs. what the passage actually says (Mark 16:8)
the_contrast.coder_saw_paraphrase: They kept silent, telling no one anything.
the_contrast.corpus_verbatim: They went out, and fled from the tomb, for trembling and astonishment had come on them. They said nothing to anyone; for they were afraid.
the_contrast.plain_caption: The retyped copy dropped 'trembling and astonishment' and 'for they were afraid' — exactly the fear the method needs to notice the women's silence. The checkout hands over the real words, so it's there.

layer_3_evidence.where_it_lives_plain: The package is a small sealed file (a snapshot you can re-open exactly). A running list of what's been checked out will become a proper table later.
layer_3_evidence.provenance: World English Bible (public domain); from library source GUT-8268

honest_limits.plain: The same passage exists two ways in the library (whole-chapter + verse-by-verse). We pick the whole-chapter one and tidy the duplicate later.
The automatic checkout (ask for any text, get a package) isn't built yet — this is a worked example for Mark.

whats_next_plain: Once 'Text' is finalized, the same drawer shape carries the next two steps: DECOMPOSE (break the passage into 'moves' — the small actions the text makes) and SITUATE (the world the text came out of).
deep_dive: the passage ladder (how Mark 16 breaks into pieces) + the library's SERVE view (the same handoff, from the library's side).
